name: Tongue pressing against roof (tongue push-ups)

lead: Tongue push-ups are a variation on mewing in which the tongue is pressed firmly against the roof of the mouth, sometimes in timed holds, with the aim of reshaping the jaws and face.

The theory is that tongue pressure on the palate guides upper jaw growth or shape. Mewing itself is associated with the orthotropics practice of John Mew and his son Mike Mew, and the American Association of Orthodontists has stated there is no evidence mewing improves the jaw. No studies were found testing this specific exercise.

paras: People practice repeated holds, or press the tongue up during the day as part of a tongue posture routine, usually as a long-term habit.
No specific harms have been documented for the exercise. Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024 after a misconduct hearing involving child patients.

angle.text: A sharper jaw and face from pressing the tongue to the palate. The theory is that tongue pressure guides jaw shape over time. Orthodontic bodies say mewing lacks evidence of jaw change, and this variant has not been studied.

lead: Tongue push-ups, or pressing the tongue against the roof of the mouth, are an active version of the tongue posture central to mewing. Practitioners hold or repeatedly press the tongue flat against the palate in the belief that the force, together with a consistent resting posture, builds a more defined jawline, a broader upper jaw and better facial structure [1].

Mewing is named after British orthodontist John Mew, who developed the oral posture approach called orthotropics with his son Mike Mew [1]. Interest rose from January 2019 according to Google Trends, spreading through YouTube, social media and looksmaxxing communities [1].

The American Association of Orthodontists has said there is no evidence that mewing improves the jaw, and Wikipedia reports that most orthodontists do not see it as an alternative to jaw surgery [1]. No studies have tested tongue push-ups specifically.

paras: The practice involves pressing the whole tongue against the palate, sometimes in timed holds, as a more deliberate form of the resting tongue posture promoted in mewing. Proponents link it to a more defined jawline and a broader upper jaw [1].

The method comes from orthotropics, developed by John Mew and his son Mike [1]. Mewing received wide media coverage after 2019 as it went viral online, and it has been popular in looksmaxxing and incel online subcultures; some students are reported to mew in class [1].

Wikipedia quotes the statement that no credible scientific research has proven the effectiveness of orthotropics, and records that the American Association of Orthodontists says there is no evidence mewing improves the jaw [1]. Mike Mew was expelled from the British Orthodontic Society and, in 2024, struck from the UK dental register after a misconduct hearing about harm to child patients [1]. A 2019 commentary in the Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery was titled 'Mewing: Social Media's Alternative to Orthognathic Surgery?' [1].
No studies found. Reviewers cited on the mewing page report that no credible research has shown orthotropics to work [1].

lore.intro: Tongue pressing is discussed in looksmaxxing spaces as part of mewing, as a stronger or more deliberate form of tongue posture.

claims.claim: Pressing the tongue hard against the palate reshapes the jaw and face
